latest_release.body:
## What's new

**TikTok lists and search that get past the posts TikTok will not play.** One
post sent without a media address used to turn a whole page of an author's posts
or a search into a 502. Those posts are TikTok Shop videos, whose media TikTok's
web API gives to nobody, guest or signed in; they now come back with their
details and no streams, and asking for one directly says so with its own error
code. Page two of a TikTok post search, empty until now, pages again. Also: the
console's single-post form takes the share text the apps copy, retention stops
rewriting the same finished tasks on every pass, and A-Bogus signing is about 9%
faster.

### Upgrading

Installed with the script on 5.1.6 or later, in the install directory:

```bash
./dtkctl upgrade
```

On 5.1.5 or earlier, `dtkctl` has no `upgrade` yet, so this once:

```bash
cd /opt/dtk && git pull           # or ~/dtk - wherever you installed it
bash install/install.sh --upgrade # install/install.zh.sh for the Chinese one
```

It checks out `v5.1.11`, pulls 5.1.11, backs the database up, migrates, restarts
and writes `DTK_IMAGE_TAG=5.1.11` into `.env` itself; there is nothing to edit.
CloakBrowser and the browser image are unchanged.

By hand:

```bash
cd /opt/dtk && git pull
export COMPOSE_ENV_FILES=.env   # without this, `image:` ignores the root .env
# DTK_IMAGE_TAG=latest needs no edit; a pinned one becomes 5.1.11 - no `v`, see the tag table
docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml pull api worker downloader transcriber
docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml build browser-rpc   # with --profile browser
docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml run --rm migrate
docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml up -d
```

No new migrations, no new settings, and API keys need nothing. Your data is
untouched.

### Added

- **`MEDIA_WITHHELD`** (403, not retryable): the post was read in full, but the
  platform gives out no media for it - today, a TikTok Shop video. Asking for
  such a post's details, or downloading it, fails with this instead of
  `UPSTREAM_CHANGED`. If your client handles error codes, treat it like
  `CONTENT_PRIVATE`: the post exists, and no retry or login gets its media.

### Changed

- **A TikTok list can hold posts without media.** Author posts, hashtag, music,
  related posts and post search return a TikTok Shop video with its details,
  `media.video: null` and no streams, instead of failing the page. If you
  download from a list, skip the posts whose media is empty. A page on which no
  post has media at all still answers `UPSTREAM_CHANGED`: that is the platform
  changing its format, not a few posts.
- **The TikTok post search cursor carries a search id**, as in
  `20:2026110807205434CD61E448A521C8F318`. Pass it back as you got it and nothing
  changes for you; if your code read it as a number, stop - the cursor has always
  been documented as opaque. A bare offset is still accepted, and TikTok answers
  it with an empty page, as before.
- **A-Bogus signing is about 9% faster.** SM3's message expansion was rewritten;
  the signatures are byte for byte the same. Nothing to do. Thanks to
  [@dexhunter](https://github.com/dexhunter) (#821).

### Fixed

- **A TikTok author's posts or a post search failed with 502 `UPSTREAM_CHANGED`**
  when one post on the page had no media address, and every other post on the
  page was lost with it (#819). See Changed. Thanks to
  [@talaon2](https://github.com/talaon2) and [@codersjj](https://github.com/codersjj).
- **Page two of a TikTok post search was always empty.** TikTok answers a later
  page only to a request that names the search it continues, and no request did;
  the cursor carries it now. Searching posts still needs a signed-in TikTok
  identity. Thanks to [@codersjj](https://github.com/codersjj).
- **A TikTok Shop video's details were a 502** asking you to report a bug, and
  downloading one failed with "retry the download", which never helps. Both say
  `MEDIA_WITHHELD` now.

Douyin_TikTok_Download_API

[English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) 🚀 A self-hosted data API for [Douyin](https://www.douyin.com), [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com) and [Bilibili](https://www.bilibili.com). One `docker compose up`, an identity pool that maintains itself, and a REST API, MCP server and web console on top. Open source, free, and it runs on your own machine — no signup, no quota, nobody else in the path. It fetches posts, authors and comments, sounds, hashtags, live rooms, trending boards and search results, downloads video and image albums **without a watermark** (it picks the clean stream the platform already publishes rather than stripping anything), and keeps what it collects in your own PostgreSQL. A video it has downloaded can be turned into text on the same machine, offline, and an AI agent can drive all of it over MCP. ## 🧩 REER — a forum for reverse engineering

reer.dev

Somewhere to put what you work out. This project exists because people wrote down how a signature was built; the forum is for the next round of that — signatures, protocols, packers, anything taken apart. Free, no advertising, and close to no rules beyond the obvious. Bilingual, English and Chinese. Register and post; nothing is gated. ## 🎬 What it looks like
One real call: paste a link, send it, get the normalised result back. The identity pool, the scheduler and the API reference it passed through on the way are all in the same console. The interface follows the browser's language, and both are written by hand rather than machine-translated. [中文界面](./screenshots/console-zh.gif) ### Try it without installing anything **** is a live instance, open to everyone. Sign in — the login page fills the demo account in for you — and use the console: the playground, the scheduler, the library, the API reference. The same account comes with an API key you can call the scraping endpoints with, shown in plaintext on the API keys page. It is read-only. Demo requests are not written to the request log or the archive, so the database of a public instance cannot be filled by strangers, and switching demo mode off ends every demo session and kills the key immediately. **Rate limit: 30 requests per 10 seconds.** Go over it and you are cooled down for 10 seconds, during which every request is refused. It is a shared instance, and the identity pool behind it is the ceiling for everybody using it at once. What the demo is for is deciding whether to run your own. It is not a service to build on — it can go down, be reset, or be switched off, and none of that will be announced. ## 🚀 v4 vs v5 v5 is a rewrite. It started from an empty branch and inherits no v4 code. v4's real problem was never a shortage of features — it was that **the API would die quietly and nobody would know**. A cookie expires, a signature algorithm changes, an endpoint gets rate-limited, and you find out when someone files an issue. v5 puts "you can see it" and "it heals itself" ahead of features. | | v4 | v5 | |---|---|---| | Where identities come from | You copy cookies out of a browser into `config.yaml` | A headless browser mints guest identities, and the pool tops itself up when usable ones run low | | How requests go out | Straight out, as they arrive | Health tiers, quantised LRU rotation, one in-flight lock per identity, a token bucket per (identity, endpoint), a circuit breaker per endpoint | | When something breaks | You wait for a bug report | One structured record per request, live health for every identity and endpoint, visible in the console | | Call style | Synchronous — send and wait | Asynchronous by default (`202` + `task_id`); add `?wait=` to go back to synchronous | | What is kept | Nothing; parsed and discarded | PostgreSQL + Redis. Everything parsed is archived, so a post deleted upstream is still here | | Access control | None; anyone can call it | API keys with scopes and roles, managed in the console | | Interface | A single PyWebIO page | A React console: identity pool, scheduler, library, downloads, logs, diagnostics | | Ways in | REST | REST, MCP and a CLI, all over the same service layer | | Signing | X-Bogus, A_Bogus | a_bogus, X-Bogus, X-Gnarly, X-Dynosaur and Bilibili's WBI in pure Python, with a browser fallback | | Deployment | `pip install -r requirements.txt` + `python start.py` | `docker compose up`, three images | | Platforms | Douyin, TikTok, Bilibili | Douyin, TikTok, Bilibili | Bilibili was the one thing that went backwards in 5.0, because it shares neither the signing nor the identity machinery with Douyin and TikTok. It is back in 5.1.6, with the two pieces of its own that needed writing: its WBI signature in pure Python, and guest identities minted over plain HTTP, so a Bilibili pool needs no browser container. ### Still on v4? v4's code stays on the [`v4` branch](https://github.com/Evil0ctal/Douyin_TikTok_Download_API/tree/v4), the image is still published, and one command brings it up: ```bash docker run -d --name dtk-v4 --restart unless-stopped \ -p 8080:80 evil0ctal/douyin_tiktok_download_api:V4.1.2 ``` Then open ; the API reference is at `/docs`. Port 8080 is deliberate — v5 binds 8000, so the two versions can run side by side on one machine. **Replace the Douyin cookie before you use it.** v4 has no identity pool, and the cookie baked into the image expired long ago, so Douyin endpoints answer `400` until you put your own in: ```bash docker cp dtk-v4:/app/crawlers/douyin/web/config.yaml ./douyin-web.yaml # replace the Cookie line with one from your browser, then save docker rm -f dtk-v4 docker run -d --name dtk-v4 --restart unless-stopped -p 8080:80 \ -v "$PWD/douyin-web.yaml:/app/crawlers/douyin/web/config.yaml" \ evil0ctal/douyin_tiktok_download_api:V4.1.2 ``` TikTok's two config files are at `/app/crawlers/tiktok/web/config.yaml` and `/app/crawlers/tiktok/app/config.yaml`, and are mounted the same way. To keep it under Compose instead, one file is enough — with `douyin-web.yaml` already copied out next to it, or Docker will create a *directory* under that name and the app will fail to read its config: ```yaml # compose.yml services: app: image: evil0ctal/douyin_tiktok_download_api:V4.1.2 container_name: dtk-v4 restart: unless-stopped ports: - "8080:80" environment: TZ: Asia/Shanghai volumes: - ./douyin-web.yaml:/app/crawlers/douyin/web/config.yaml ``` ```bash docker rm -f dtk-v4 # the container from the run above holds the name docker compose -p dtk-v4 up -d ``` `main` is v5 now and `latest` is the newest v5 release — it moves when a release is cut, never on a push to `main` — so **pin the tag to stay on v4**. `V4.1.2` is the last v4 release; the branch merged a few PRs after it (Bilibili downloads, cookie hot-reload), and that code is published under the commit tag `5be4838`. There is no guided installer for v4 — the script in Quick start below installs v5. What is above is all v4 gets: the branch still takes PRs, but nothing new is built on it, and a fresh install should start on v5. ### Building this together There are a few group chats around my open-source projects. If you want to work on this one, or just talk shop, add me on WeChat at **`Evil0ctal`** with the note **github 交流** and I will add you. The groups are for learning from each other. **No advertising and nothing illegal** — they are for making friends and talking about the work. ## 📦 What it can fetch | Capability | Douyin | TikTok | Bilibili | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:| | One post (video or image album) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Author profile | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | An author's posts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | An author's liked posts | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | | Mixes / playlists / seasons, and an author's list of them | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Comments | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Comment replies | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Public folders and what is in them | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | A video's parts, for one uploaded in several | — | — | ✅ | | The site's popular boards: hot, weekly, all-time picks, top 100 | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Followers | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | | Following | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | | Posts recommended beside a post | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | A sound, and the posts that use it | ✅ | ✅ | — | | A hashtag | ✅ | ✅ | — | | The posts under a hashtag | ❌ | ✅ | — | | Keyword search: posts and accounts | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | A live room: whether it is on, and its pull URLs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | A live room by its broadcast's own id, and Douyin app share links | ✅ | ✅ | — | | Whether many live rooms are on air, in one call | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | | A live room's audience ranking | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | Trending boards | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | Douyin serves its follower and following lists only to a signed-in session, so those two endpoints are not registered at all: an endpoint that always returns an empty page is worth nothing. Search and the posts under a hashtag are the same story: Douyin refuses both to a guest, and no signed-in answer has been measured yet, so neither is offered there. On TikTok the account search answers a guest, while the post search refuses one outright (measured 2026-11-02), so an imported login is what it takes. Importing your own logged-in cookies widens what the rest can see, too. On Bilibili that matters most for comments: a guest is shown the three hottest and no more, so an imported login is what turns that into the full thread. On Douyin it decides an author's liked posts outright: a guest is shown none, public or not, so that list needs a logged-in identity in the pool. An imported login is used at your own risk: platforms rarely ban an account for reading data with it, but a ban cannot be ruled out ([what to know before importing one](documents/en/06-identities-and-proxies.md#a-logged-in-jar-is-not-a-guest-identity)). The dashes are not gaps: a Douyin or TikTok post is never more than one video, so it has no parts to list, and a Bilibili live room has one number for good rather than an id per broadcast. Media downloads, the content archive, counter snapshots, collections and a watchlist are built in; none of them needs another service. ## 🤖 Let an AI agent use it: MCP Point Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, Cherry Studio or any other MCP client at `/mcp` on your own instance, and the agent can read posts, authors and comments, store a post's media and transcribe it. It goes through the same service layer, identity pool and scheduler as the REST API, and an API key's scopes bound what it may do. ```bash claude mcp add --transport http dtk http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/ \ --header "Authorization: Bearer dtk_YOUR_API_KEY" ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `parse_url` | Fetch whatever a link points at — a post, an author, a short link, pasted share text | | `get_video` · `get_user` | One post, or one author profile, by id | | `list_user_posts` · `list_comments` | An author's posts or a post's comments, a page at a time | | `get_content_history` | The recorded counter history of a post or an author, from the local database | | `pool_status` | Identity-pool and endpoint health, so an agent can tell "try later" from "broken" | | `download_media` | Store a post's media on this instance | | `transcribe_video` | Turn a stored video into text | | `get_task_result` | Collect a result that did not finish within the call | Ten tools, and few on purpose: every extra tool makes an agent worse at picking the right one, so a new capability arrives as an argument to an existing tool. Setup for each client, and what every tool returns: [MCP and AI agents](./documents/en/12-mcp.md). The console shows the same guide at `/mcp-guide`. ## 🎙 Speech to text, on your own machine A downloaded video can be transcribed where it is stored. FunASR models — Paraformer for the speech, FSMN-VAD to find where someone is talking, CT-Transformer for punctuation — run in a sidecar on a network with no route out, so the audio never leaves the host and no API is called. - **Where:** the **Transcriptions** page in the console, a **Transcribe video** button on every finished download, the **Library** (one stored post, or a whole selection at once), `POST /api/v1/transcriptions`, or the `transcribe_video` MCP tool - **What you get:** one whole text per video, with numbers written as digits, exportable as `.txt` - **How fast:** a 3 min 13 s clip took 3.7 seconds on two CPU cores; no GPU needed - **What it is good at:** Mandarin. The models are the general Chinese ones, so other languages come out poorly It is off by default. The guided installer asks, then downloads the ~500 MB of models and checks each file against its SHA-256; by hand, see [Preparing the FunASR ONNX models](./documents/en/18-funasr-models.md) and [Turning a stored video into text](./documents/en/08-downloads-and-library.md#turning-a-stored-video-into-text). ## 🔗 Which links it accepts Paste whatever you have — a short link, a post URL, or the whole caption a platform app puts on your clipboard: ``` https://v.douyin.com/L4NpDJ6/ https://www.douyin.com/video/7126745726494821640 https://www.douyin.com/jingxuan?modal_id=7660875690212492466 https://www.tiktok.com/@evil0ctal/video/7156033831819037994 https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTR9nkkmL/ 2.84 nqe:/ https://v.douyin.com/L4FJNR3/ https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c7mD https://www.bilibili.com/video/av170001 https://b23.tv/ https://space.bilibili.com/2 ``` Short links are followed and a link buried in a caption is extracted. A post id is also checked against the platform's own encoding first, so an id that cannot exist is refused here rather than costing an upstream request. A Bilibili av number is turned into the bvid it stands for, so either spelling reaches the same post. ## ⚗️ Built with | | | |---|---| | Service | Python 3.12 · FastAPI · SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async) · Alembic · Typer · structlog | | Transport | wreq (browser TLS fingerprint emulation) · httpx | | Data | PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB · Redis | | Console | React 19 · TypeScript · Vite · TanStack Query · wouter · i18next | | Signing | a_bogus, X-Bogus, X-Gnarly, X-Dynosaur and Bilibili's WBI in pure Python | | Identity minting | CloakBrowser, headless, in a container of its own, called over HTTP; Bilibili guests over plain HTTP, no browser | | Downloader | Go 1.23, standard library only, statically linked into a scratch image | | Transcription | FunASR ONNX (Paraformer, FSMN-VAD, CT-Transformer), offline, in a container with no network route | | Auth | argon2id password hashing · API keys with scopes | | Protocols | REST (OpenAPI) · MCP (streamable-http) · CLI | | Tooling | uv · ruff · mypy · pytest · Docker Compose | Nothing beyond Postgres and Redis is required. No Kafka, no Elasticsearch, no object store, no Kubernetes. CloakBrowser is pinned to a specific commit. That pin is a security control — see [docker/Dockerfile.browser](./docker/Dockerfile.browser). ## 🗂 Project layout **First, what `dtk` is.** `Douyin_TikTok_Download_API` is a mouthful, so the code says **DTK** instead: **D**ouyin + **T**i**K**Tok. The two platforms, and not the download or API halves of the name. It is the Python package (`src/dtk/`), the command (`dtk --help`), the prefix on every environment variable (`DTK_SECRET_KEY` and friends), the Compose project name (`-p dtk`), and the three letters in the console's title bar. Where you see `dtk`, it means `Douyin_TikTok_Download_API`. ``` Douyin_TikTok_Download_API/ ├── src/dtk/ the service; all of it lives here │ ├── api/ FastAPI routes, auth, OpenAPI localisation │ ├── platforms/ Douyin, TikTok and Bilibili adapters: endpoints, params, parsers │ ├── signing/ a_bogus / X-Bogus / X-Gnarly / X-Dynosaur / WBI │ ├── transport/ outbound requests, response classification │ ├── identity/ identity minting and health │ ├── scheduler/ identity selection, token buckets, circuit breakers │ ├── services/ the business layer, shared by REST, MCP and the CLI │ ├── worker/ async tasks, callbacks, scheduled collection │ ├── db/ SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migrations │ ├── ops/ diagnostics, backups, health checks, alerting │ ├── media/ downloader client │ ├── models/ one content model across every platform │ ├── urls/ link recognition, short-link expansion, id validation │ ├── mcp/ MCP server │ ├── cli/ the dtk command line │ ├── i18n/ server-side English and Chinese strings │ └── core/ settings, logging, error types ├── web/ the React console, built into the app image │ └── src/ │ ├── pages/ one file per console page │ ├── components/ design system and shared components │ └── locales/ console English and Chinese strings ├── docker/ four Dockerfiles, compose, and three sidecars │ ├── browser_rpc/ Python, wrapping CloakBrowser │ ├── downloader/ Go, the media download sidecar │ ├── transcriber/ Python, offline FunASR transcription │ └── compose.yml ├── documents/ user documentation, 18 pages in each language ├── tests/ unit / integration / contract / replay ├── scripts/ smoke.sh ├── .github/workflows/ CI and Docker image publishing ├── alembic.ini ├── pyproject.toml └── Makefile ``` ## ⚡️ Quick start: self-host it with Docker If you would rather not think about it, the guided script asks a few questions and brings the stack up — it works out your distribution, checks for Docker, and scales the resource limits to the machine: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Evil0ctal/Douyin_TikTok_Download_API/main/install/install.sh -o install.sh less install.sh # reading it first is a good habit bash install.sh ``` **Afterwards the same script is the operations tool.** Run it again and it finds the install and opens a menu: status, upgrade (compared against the latest GitHub release), passwords, an extra administrator, backup and restore, runtime settings, disk cleanup, stop or uninstall. `--manage` goes straight there. Details in [install/README.md](./install/README.md). The manual route follows. There are two ways to install this; below is the recommended one. For the by-hand route, see [Without Docker](#without-docker). | How | Who for | Full steps | |---|---|---| | **Docker Compose** (recommended) | Almost everyone, production included | [Installation · First install](./documents/en/02-installation.md#first-install) | | By hand | Docker is not an option, or you are changing the code | [For development](./documents/en/02-installation.md#running-without-docker) · [On bare metal](./documents/en/02-installation.md#a-production-install-without-docker) | > **Installing from mainland China?** Switch your mirrors before you start, or the pull will > most likely time out: > [Network preparation in mainland China](./documents/en/02-installation.md#network-preparation-in-mainland-china). You need Docker and Docker Compose. Start by cloning the repository — the compose file, the Dockerfiles and the migrations all live in it, and the default branch is v5: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Evil0ctal/Douyin_TikTok_Download_API.git cd Douyin_TikTok_Download_API ``` Nothing in the repository ships a default password or key, so write `.env` next: ```bash POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24) REDIS_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24) cat > .env < and use the token from the log to create the first administrator. That starts no browser container, and without it (`--profile browser`, see [the optional profiles](./documents/en/02-installation.md#the-optional-profiles)) Douyin and TikTok identities can only be imported, not minted: both hand a visitor its cookies from inside their page scripts. Bilibili guests are minted over plain HTTP either way. ### Where the image comes from By default it is built locally: the first `up` compiles the application image from the Dockerfile in this repository, which takes a few minutes. To skip that, point compose at the published image instead, in the same `.env`: ```bash cat >> .env <<'EOF' DTK_IMAGE=evil0ctal/douyin_tiktok_download_api DTK_IMAGE_TAG=latest EOF export COMPOSE_ENV_FILES=.env docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml pull docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml up -d ``` These two are read by compose itself rather than by the containers, and compose looks for them in `docker/.env` unless `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` says otherwise. Without the export it finds nothing, falls back to the local names and quietly builds from source again, so it belongs in every shell you run compose from. The script's `dtkctl` carries it for you. `latest` is the newest release and moves only when one is cut, so updating later needs nothing edited here. The `pull` is not optional: these services declare both `image` and `build`, so compose builds from the local Dockerfile whenever the image is not already on the machine rather than reaching for a registry. Images are published for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, so Apple Silicon and a Raspberry Pi both run natively. The browser container is not published: it installs CloakBrowser from a pinned commit, and that pin is a security control that should be yours to choose, so it stays a local build. ### Without Docker Supported, and it is how the project itself is developed. You provide PostgreSQL 17 (**with the TimescaleDB extension** — a plain `postgres:17` will not do), Redis 8, Python 3.12 and uv, plus Node 22 if you build the console. client setup at `/mcp-guide` in the console | | CLI | `dtk --help` | Same | The main capabilities: - **Parse** a link, share text, short link, or a bare post id - **Archive** everything parsed, so a post deleted upstream is still here - **Download** media to your own disk, in bulk by author, skipping what you have, with duplicate cleanup - **Transcribe** a stored video to text, offline - **Watch** an author or a post and re-collect it on a timer - **iOS Shortcut** support at `/api/v1/ios/shortcut` ## 🔄 Updating to a new release The console keeps an eye out for you: `system.check_updates` is on by default, and if a newer release exists you get one notice after signing in, at most once a day. That request goes from **your browser** to GitHub — the server never sends anything outward, so it does not tell anyone this instance exists. Turn it off in Settings if you would rather it did not. If you installed with the script, it is one command in the install directory: ```bash cd /opt/dtk # or ~/dtk - wherever you installed it ./dtkctl upgrade # the latest release; ./dtkctl upgrade 5.1.6 for a given one ``` It moves the checkout to the release's tag, pulls the new images (or rebuilds them, on an install built from source), rebuilds the browser image, takes a backup, migrates, and only then writes the version it moved to into `.env` and restarts. Anything that fails before the restart puts the checkout and `.env` back, and the old version keeps running. There is nothing to edit by hand. An install from before 5.1.6 does not have `upgrade` yet; there, once, run `git pull && bash install/install.sh --upgrade` in the same directory, and from then on it is `./dtkctl upgrade`. Running `bash install.sh --manage` and picking 2 does the same from the menu. By hand it is: ```bash cd /opt/dtk && git pull export COMPOSE_ENV_FILES=.env # Running the published images (recommended). Name the services you run: # add downloader and transcriber if you enabled them, with the same --profile flags. docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml pull api worker docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml build browser-rpc # only with --profile browser docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml run --rm migrate docker compose -p dtk -f docker/compose.yml up -d ``` With `DTK_IMAGE_TAG=latest` there is nothing to change first. A checkout the script made sits on a release tag, where `git pull` has no branch to pull: there, use `git fetch origin tag v5.1.7 && git checkout --detach v5.1.7`. Building locally instead? Swap `pull` for `build`. `migrate` runs on every start and Alembic is idempotent, so running it separately is only about getting the schema up before the containers switch over. **Your data stays put.** The named volumes (`postgres-data`, `redis-data`, `media-data`) survive a rebuild, so the identity pool, the archive, the settings and the API keys are all where you left them. The browser image is built from this checkout, never pulled, so rebuild it on every update: under a tag that stays the same - `latest`, or a local build's `dev` - the old one keeps running the old code. Cached layers keep it short. To go back, `./dtkctl upgrade 5.1.5` with the script, or set `DTK_IMAGE_TAG` to the previous version or `sha-` by hand and `up -d` again. Migrations have no automatic downgrade, so the script refuses, before pulling anything, a release that lacks the database's latest migration; past one, the way back is a new install of the old version with a backup taken on it restored. Back the database up before upgrading — the script does — which is the only rollback that always works. ## 📖 Documentation **Read it online at [douyin.wtf](https://douyin.wtf)** — the same 18 pages, rendered, searchable and in both languages.
